title: Hybrid Reasoning: Where the LLM Boundary Belongs

steps.prompt: A Returns subagent must confirm an order is within its 30-day return window before offering a return label. Customers then explain what went wrong in their own words, and the agent must interpret each explanation to pick a return reason. How should the architect split this work between logic and the LLM?

options.label: Code the 30-day check as Agent Script logic and handle explanations with prompt instructions
options.rationale: The hybrid model routes a decision through the LLM only when it needs judgment or interpretation; anything expressible as code runs deterministically. A date comparison is code, while free-form explanations span too many inputs to anticipate with conditions.

options.label: Describe both the 30-day check and the explanation handling in prompt instructions
options.rationale: Leaving the date check to the LLM makes a fixed rule probabilistic, so some out-of-window orders can still receive a return label.

options.label: Code the 30-day check and every expected explanation as if-else branches in Agent Script
options.rationale: Customer explanations vary too widely for conditional branches, so any wording the tree did not anticipate falls through without a return reason.

options.label: Ground the subagent in the returns policy article and let the LLM apply the 30-day rule
options.rationale: Grounding gives the LLM the policy text but still leaves the date comparison to model judgment, so the rule is not guaranteed to hold.
